title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 112
paragraphs: Once they were in place and the sacrifices proved favorable, the Athenians were released and set off at a run to attack the barbarians. The space between the armies was no less than eight stades. The Persians, seeing them coming at a run, prepared to receive them, convinced in their own minds that the Athenians were suicidally insane, given how few they were and that they were pressing forward on the run without any cavalry or archers. So the barbarians thought. But the Athenians, when in full body they crashed into the enemy, fought in a memorable fashion. They were the first of all the Greeks I know of to charge the enemy at a run, and the first to endure the sight of Median clothing and the men who wore it — for up to that time even the very name of the Medes had been a terror to Greek ears.
